correctness.rationale: Exact finite claim for rational points of PG(2,3), no extension-plane generality. There are 13 points, 13 four-point lines, and exactly 234 four-arcs. The graph joins four-arcs with three common points; each has 12 neighbors, giving 1404 edges. Every exchange changes target intersection by at most one, establishing lower bound 4-|A∩B|. The two actual package verifiers independently construct plane incidence from homogeneous determinant coordinates and from 9 affine points plus 4 infinity directions, test all 715 four-sets, BFS from all 234 ovals, and check all 27,261 unordered pairs. A separately coded finite-plane enumeration re-derived all distances and the equivalence of precisely one extra step with A∪B meeting every line without containing any line; histogram (3,1):1404,(2,2):7020,(2,3):702,(1,3):12636,(1,4):936,(0,4):4563; spheres (1,12,60,114,47), diameter 4, and 1638 exceptional pairs. Complete finite enumeration is a proof for this finite domain, not an inferred infinite classification. Each oval has six exceptional partners at common pairs and eight at common singletons.
